hints: Find perpendicular tangent gradient $m = 2$ and form line equation through $B(3, 2)$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the gradient of the radius segment $AB$:
$$m_{AB} = \frac{2 - 4}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{-2}{4} = -\frac{1}{2}$$

Determine the gradient of the tangent line perpendicular to $AB$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\frac{1}{-1/2} = 2$$

Write the equation of the tangent line passing through $B(3, 2)$:
$$y - 2 = 2(x - 3) \implies y = 2x - 4$$

hints: Write the circle equation with centre $B(3, 2)$.
walkthrough:
Write down the equation of the circle centred at $B(3, 2)$:
$$(x - 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 20$$

Substitute the tangent relation $(y - 2) = 2(x - 3)$ into the circle equation:
$$(x - 3)^2 + (2(x - 3))^2 = 20 \implies (x - 3)^2 + 4(x - 3)^2 = 20$$
$$5(x - 3)^2 = 20 \implies (x - 3)^2 = 4$$

Solve for the $x$-coordinates of points $C$ and $D$:
$$x - 3 = \pm 2$$
$$x = 3 - 2 = 1 \quad \text{and} \quad x = 3 + 2 = 5$$
$$(\text{Solutions: } x = 1, \quad x = 5)$$
